chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Ben Webster's character
summary: Collins met Ben in Chicago in the early thirties, calls him warm and unique, and says he turned violent and could not play when drinking.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: You said you appeared opposite Fats. You were playing with whom?
With Roy Eldridge, yes. Yes, we were --
Fats Waller had a big band and Roy Eldridge (inaudible) on the same bill?
That's right, yeah, yeah, in the Howard Theatre in Washington. Had some great shows then. Ben Webster.

Well, I loved Ben. Ben as you know Ben was one of the greats, you know, and I've known -- I met Ben -- I'm trying to think. Was Ben -- I think I met Ben -- that was in the early thirties, in Chicago, and he would play around then. Then he was with -- I'm trying to think if he left Fletcher to go with Cab or if he left Cab to go with Fletcher. But he got into some trouble around Chicago about a woman, you know, and he had to leave town so he changed jobs with Chu Chew, I believe, Chu Berry. Because of that. But Ben was -- there was only one Ben. You know, he's a very warm person, but an individualist, you know. And one thing he couldn't do was drink. He would get violent when he drank. You saw --
I remember, but was it he was always that way? It was when I knew him, but I didn't know him until the late forties.
Always, he's always been. He never could drink, and he couldn't play neither.
When he drank he couldn't play either. You know, the world's worst when he drank. You know, you'd walk out on him.
